newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-BICC SEES BETTER H2 PERFORMANCE.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-BICC SEES BETTER H2 PERFORMANCE.

text.p: BICC Plc, the UK cables to construction group, expects to deliver an improved performance in the second half, mostly fuelled by its construction division Balfour Beatty.

Alan Jones, chief executive, told Reuters in an interview that thanks to Balfour Beatty's progress and its efforts to rationalise its loss-making power cables division in Germany and Italy, the next six months would be better.

Part of the improvement would come also from enhanced cost savings thanks to the job cuts planned for Germany and Italy. Savings currently stand at 40 million stg per annum, but that figure is seen growing by the year end, said Jones.
The chief executive said 350 jobs would be axed in Italy, reducing the workforce form its current level of 1,230.

But BICC remains silent on how many jobs will go in Germany. "We can't say at the moment," he said. An update is expected shortly, said Jones. The German power cables division employs 700 people and has seen its workforce slashed from over 2000.
"In Germany our competitors are also reducing their capacity. It's sensible progress," said Jones.
Commenting on other divisions, he said extra high voltage cables, which showed almost no profit in the first half, would "show a lot more profit in the second half" as a strong order book kicks in.
The Australian business is also seen showing an improved performance in the latter part of the year, said Jones as restructuring efforts begin to pay off.
On capital expenditure, BICC said it expected to "more than double" interim period investment of 65 million by the year end.
